Context/Background:
Tumor-infiltrating B cells play a significant role in tumor development, progression, and prognosis, yet a comprehensive classification system is lacking. To address this gap, we present a pan-cancer single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas of tumor-infiltrating B and plasma cells across a large sample cohort. 

We isolated B cells and plasma cells from 15 studies spanning 7 cancer types as data sources. After applying batch correction and integrating the data, we removed low-quality cells and determined the optimal number of clusters. Using standard Seurat methods for integration, clustering, and differential expression analysis, we confirmed the absence of batch effects, with no study- or cancer type-specific clusters. 

We employed a graph-based clustering method to identify TIL-Bs with recurring phenotypes, uncovering a total of 10 clusters. Step one of cluster annotation used canonical markers like CD19 and MS4A1 (CD20), which are prevalent throughout B cell development but decline in plasma cells. Markers such as CD38, JCHAIN, and SDC1 (CD138) are prominent in plasma cells, but less so in earlier stages. This revealed four B cell clusters, two intermediate clusters with proliferative and germinal center (GC) features, and four plasma cell clusters.
Prompt: Based on upregulated pathways and differentially expressed markers in each cluster, assign functional phenotypes to each of the 4 B-cell clusters (clusters 1-4).  Provide a discussion of the reasoning behind cluster assignments, highlighting important genes and pathways where relevant.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
A pan-cancer scRNA-seq atlas was generated from tumor-infiltrating B cells (TIL-Bs) across seven cancer types (15 studies). Standard Seurat integration and graph-based clustering yielded 10 clusters: four B-cell clusters (1–4), two intermediate proliferative/GC‐like, and four plasma cell clusters. Canonical B-cell markers (CD19, MS4A1/CD20) extend through clusters 1–4; plasma markers (CD38, JCHAIN, SDC1/CD138) define separate clusters. Here we focus on clusters 1–4, all CD19⁺MS4A1⁺ B cells. Dataset details (replicates, exact sample numbers) are not specified.  

Keywords  
• Antigen presentation  
• NF-κB/TNF signaling  
• Interferon response  

Candidate Genes  
• HLA-DRB5  
• CD86  
• CD83  
• TCL1A  
• CD69  

Cluster phenotypes and reasoning  
Cluster 2 – Naïve/resting B cells  
• Marker profile: modest upregulation of BLK (BCR‐associated tyrosine kinase), LY86 (MD-1), LTB (lymphotoxin β).  
• Enrichment (ORA): “Allograft rejection” (MSigDB_Hallmark; LTB, LY86), IL-6/JAK/STAT3 and NF-κB signaling (via LTB) at nominal FDR < 0.05.  
Interpretation: low‐magnitude differential expression of tonic BCR‐signaling kinases and lymphotoxin suggests a resting/naïve phenotype prior to antigen encounter.  

Cluster 1 – Follicular/memory-like B cells  
• Top DE markers: TCL1A (naïve/memory B-cell survival), FCER2/CD23 (low-affinity IgE receptor), CD72 (B-cell co-receptor), GPR183/EBI2 (follicular positioning), HLA-DRB5/DPB1 (antigen presentation).  
• Enrichment (ORA): Myc Targets V1 (strong FDR ~ 1.4 × 10⁻⁷), multiple KEGG autoimmune/antigen-presentation pathways (e.g., “Intestinal immune network for IgA production,” “Antigen processing and presentation”; HLA-DP/DR genes).  
Interpretation: Myc‐driven metabolism with high HLA-class II, CD23 and GPR183 indicate a follicular memory-cell state poised for rapid re-activation.  

Cluster 4 – Activated/pre-germinal center B cells  
• Marker profile: early activation receptors (CD69, CD83), homing/migration (CCR7, CXCR5), NF-κB modulators (REL, NFKBID, BCL2A1) and transcription factors (FOXP1, IRF8, JUNB).  
• Enrichment (GSEA, MSigDB_Hallmark): TNF-α Signaling via NF-κB (NES ≈ 2.88, FDR = 0.016), Inflammatory Response (NES ≈ 2.18, FDR = 0.059).  
Interpretation: CCR7⁺CD83⁺CD69⁺ profile with elevated NF-κB and inflammatory‐response pathways typifies early activation and transit from T-cell zones toward germinal centers.  

Cluster 3 – Interferon-activated antigen-presenting B cells  
• Marker profile: costimulatory molecule CD86, HLA-DPA1/DPB1, SPIB (B-cell TF), multiple IFN-stimulated genes (IFI44L, IFITM1, OAS1, GBP4, XAF1), cytoskeletal regulators (ARPC1B, CAPG).  
• Enrichment (GSEA, GO_BP & Hallmark): Interferon Gamma Response (NES ≈ 2.99, FDR = 0.008), Interferon Alpha Response (NES ≈ 2.60, FDR = 0.014), Defense Response to Virus, Cytokine Signaling in Immune System. ORA confirms IFN signatures.  
Interpretation: a highly activated, innate-like B-cell subset with strong IFN-driven antiviral and antigen-presentation programs, likely serving as APC-competent effectors within the tumor microenvironment.  

—  
Each cluster’s phenotype aligns with its top DE markers and pathway enrichments: cluster 2 as resting/naïve, cluster 1 as follicular memory, cluster 4 as early activated/pre-GC, and cluster 3 as interferon-activated APC-like effector B cells.
